question: What problem arises if capacity is imagined as separate from the power-holder?
premises: One might posit capacity as distinct.
Distinct positing requires naming and delimiting it.
inference: If capacity were imagined separately, it would lead only to an endless proliferation of names.
uncertainties: The exact force of vā here may indicate an alternative formulation of the same fault.
plain_english: If capacity were imagined as separate, there would be only an endless multiplication of names for it.
